title: DGCR8 Mediates Repair of UV-Induced DNA Damage Independently of RNA Processing
central_claims: UV-induced DGCR8 S153 phosphorylation mediates transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair and UV resistance independently of RNA processing; JNK contributes to phosphorylation.

source_manifest.title: DGCR8 regulates multiple processes of transcription coupled nucleotide excision repair
source_manifest.finding: Genome-edited endogenous S153A cells and mouse fibroblasts impair UV-induced TC-NER interactions; identifies R-loop and checkpoint roles. Shares senior author Taniguchi with original.

source_manifest.title: Non-canonical function of DGCR8 in DNA double-strand break repair signaling and tumor radioresistance
source_manifest.finding: Independent team extends noncanonical DGCR8 repair to ionizing radiation through ATM/S677, USP51 and RNF168. This is a different lesion and phosphorylation site, not reproduction of UV/S153/TC-NER.

source_manifest.title: Regulation of the microprocessor by post-translational modifications
source_manifest.finding: Independent review explicitly retains JNK/S153-dependent UV resistance through TC-NER and RNA-processing independence, while noting overexpression and in-vivo limitations.

answers.rationale: No independent primary study read directly tests the full UV/S153/TC-NER claim. The 2021 independent paper establishes a related but distinct S677/double-strand-break mechanism.
The direct 2026 UV follow-up shares the original senior investigator; the independent 2021 result concerns different lesions and phosphorylation.

Endogenous genome-edited S153A human cells and primary mutant mouse fibroblasts extend the original depletion/complementation evidence: UV-induced repair-complex interactions depend on S153. This is a stricter mechanistic test, though not independent and not a full repeat of lesion-removal assays.

evidence.explanation: Endogenous genome-edited S153A human cells and primary mutant mouse fibroblasts extend the original depletion/complementation evidence: UV-induced repair-complex interactions depend on S153. This is a stricter mechanistic test, though not independent and not a full repeat of lesion-removal assays.

answers.rationale: The independent 2025 microprocessor review retains the specific S153/JNK, UV-resistance, TC-NER and RNA-processing-independent finding.

evidence.explanation: The independent 2025 microprocessor review retains the specific S153/JNK, UV-resistance, TC-NER and RNA-processing-independent finding.

answers.rationale: Later mechanistic work addresses unresolved interactions, but the stated kinase redundancy and organismal/pathological relevance limitations have not been explicitly tested as a package demonstrating retained usefulness.

Hang and colleagues explicitly build from the noncanonical UV-repair finding to test a different DNA-damage mechanism, identifying ATM/S677-dependent double-strand-break repair. The extension does not validate every UV-specific claim.

evidence.explanation: Hang and colleagues explicitly build from the noncanonical UV-repair finding to test a different DNA-damage mechanism, identifying ATM/S677-dependent double-strand-break repair. The extension does not validate every UV-specific claim.

answers.rationale: One independent substantive experimental extension was established; the direct 2026 extension is not a second independent group.

The independent study operationalizes the original separation of DGCR8 repair from Drosha binding using wild-type versus Drosha-binding-deficient complementation in radiation-response experiments; substantive reuse of the noncanonical framework, not reuse of a newly invented mutant.

evidence.explanation: The independent study operationalizes the original separation of DGCR8 repair from Drosha binding using wild-type versus Drosha-binding-deficient complementation in radiation-response experiments; substantive reuse of the noncanonical framework, not reuse of a newly invented mutant.

answers.rationale: The review recognizes noncanonical functions but does not explicitly attribute an enabled research direction to this particular paper.
No independent baseline or reference-construction comparison of the original UV-repair contribution was located.

Applying the noncanonical DGCR8 repair framework independently yields a distinct ATM/S677–USP51–RNF168 mechanism and experimental radioresistance results. Clinical treatment benefit is not established.

evidence.explanation: Applying the noncanonical DGCR8 repair framework independently yields a distinct ATM/S677–USP51–RNF168 mechanism and experimental radioresistance results. Clinical treatment benefit is not established.

answers.rationale: The RNA-processing-independent DGCR8 repair framework is successfully extended from UV lesions to ionizing-radiation double-strand-break responses. It does not establish transfer of S153-mediated TC-NER to that setting.

evidence.explanation: The RNA-processing-independent DGCR8 repair framework is successfully extended from UV lesions to ionizing-radiation double-strand-break responses. It does not establish transfer of S153-mediated TC-NER to that setting.

answers.rationale: The original S153/TC-NER finding enables targeted genome editing and new observations of repair-complex assembly, R-loop regulation and CHK1 activation.

evidence.explanation: The original S153/TC-NER finding enables targeted genome editing and new observations of repair-complex assembly, R-loop regulation and CHK1 activation.

answers.rationale: Potential disease relevance and radiosensitization experiments do not establish operational use of this UV-repair finding in a clinical workflow or other practice.
This is a mechanistic biological discovery without a proposed competing method or claimed comparative performance advantage; UV resistance is the biological outcome, not a method advantage.
The direct mechanistic extension uses the original S153 finding in 2026, nine years after publication.

evidence.explanation: The direct mechanistic extension uses the original S153 finding in 2026, nine years after publication.

answers.rationale: The independent 2025 synthesis positively retains the specific UV-repair contribution more than three years later, with mechanistic and experimental limitations.

evidence.explanation: The independent 2025 synthesis positively retains the specific UV-repair contribution more than three years later, with mechanistic and experimental limitations.

answers.rationale: Independent substantive primary follow-up was established for 2021 only; the 2025 review is assessment and the 2026 experiment shares an original investigator.
The independent microprocessor post-translational-modification synthesis includes this specific noncanonical UV-repair mechanism as an established function.

evidence.explanation: The independent microprocessor post-translational-modification synthesis includes this specific noncanonical UV-repair mechanism as an established function.

answers.rationale: Continued mechanistic use is documented, but no source explicitly tests its usefulness despite newer alternatives.

search_gaps: No independent direct UV/S153 reproduction or explicit refutation located; absence is not proof of no replication.
The independent double-strand-break extension is not treated as support of the entire original central claim.
No operational or in-vivo disease benefit of the original UV mechanism established.
research.summary: Specific UV-repair mechanism retained in a 2025 independent synthesis and investigated more strictly by a same-investigator 2026 follow-up. Independent 2021 work substantively extends the noncanonical DGCR8 framework to a different damage pathway. Direct independent reproduction and clinical utility remain unresolved.
